# fingerprintd usage guide for AI agents

`fingerprintd` is a server-authoritative device-fingerprinting service for
anti-fraud and anti-automation. The client only collects evidence; the server
issues a one-time challenge, fuzzy-matches the evidence against its fingerprint
library, fuses passive network signals, and returns `visitor_id` + `confidence` +
`decision` under a `request_id`. The identity is never computed on the client, so
it cannot be forged or replayed. The customer backend reads the authoritative
result server-to-server with `GET /events/{request_id}`.

Primary docs:

- README: https://github.com/WuChenDi/fingerprintd/blob/main/README.md
- Design spec: https://github.com/WuChenDi/fingerprintd/blob/main/DESIGN.md
- Repository: https://github.com/WuChenDi/fingerprintd

## What it is

- One compute engine (`crates/fp-core`, published on crates.io as `fingerprintd`), two deployment targets: a native Axum
  server (`crates/fingerprintd`) and a Cloudflare Worker (`apps/edge`, running
  `fp-core` compiled to WASM). A client works against either unchanged.
- A pure-TypeScript browser SDK (`@cdlab/fingerprintd`) wraps FingerprintJS/BotD
  and the known-answer integrity probes, and submits — it never derives an id.
- A browser playground (`apps/web`) drives the full flow and visualizes what the
  client sends vs. what the server judges.
- A risk route on the edge Worker (`apps/edge`, `POST /checkin/assess`, Bearer
  `FP_API_KEY`, body `{ account_id, action, request_id }`) scores a stored
  `/identify` event plus its own account/device/IP/time aggregation for check-in
  anti-farming — the reference example of turning fingerprintd signals into an
  allow/challenge/deny decision without modifying the core; the playground
  (`apps/web`) demos it.

## The flow

1. `GET /challenge` — the server mints a one-time nonce (short TTL, single-use)
   and returns `{ nonce, expires_in }`.
2. The client collects `components` (a closed schema: canvas / webgl / fonts /
   audio / screen / …, the identity-matching input), plus the optional
   `user_agent`, `botd` verdict and `integrity` probe verdicts (risk signals only).
3. `POST /identify { nonce, ts, components, user_agent?, botd?, integrity? }` —
   the server checks `ts` against its skew window, burns the nonce (replay
   protection), recalls candidates by blocking keys, scores them with the
   Fellegi–Sunter model, fuses passive JA4/IP signals, and returns the result
   with a fresh `request_id`. This browser-side response is display-only.
4. The customer backend calls `GET /events/{request_id}` with
   `Authorization: Bearer <FP_API_KEY>` and gates on that authoritative result.

## Endpoints

Both stacks serve the same wire contract (all JSON snake_case):

- `GET /health` — liveness (`200 OK`).
- `GET /challenge` — issue a one-time nonce challenge.
- `POST /identify` — compute `visitor_id` + `confidence` + `decision`. The request
  body is a closed schema: an unknown key at any level, a wrong type or malformed
  JSON is `400` (`415` for a non-JSON content type). A reused/expired nonce, or a
  `ts` outside the skew window, returns `401`.
- `GET /events/{request_id}` — the stored identify body, server-to-server. Gated
  by `api_key` / `FP_API_KEY` (route `404` when unset, `401` on a wrong bearer);
  unknown or expired ids are `404`.
- `DELETE /visitor/{visitor_id}` — GDPR erasure of the visitor and its events.
  Gated by `admin_key` / `FP_ADMIN_KEY` (route `404` when unset); idempotent
  (`204` even if the visitor did not exist).

`/identify` (and `/events/{request_id}`) returns:

```json
{
  "request_id": "string",
  "visitor_id": "string",
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "decision": "match | review | new_device",
  "is_new_device": false,
  "collision_risk": false,
  "signals": {
    "ua_tls_consistent": true,
    "ip_risk": "low | medium | high",
    "client_integrity": "ok | noise | unavailable",
    "persona_coherence": "consistent | mismatch | unknown",
    "new_device_velocity": "low | medium | high",
    "automation": "detected | not_detected | unknown",
    "template_jump": false
  }
}
```

`confidence` is DECISION confidence, not identity trust: a brand-new device
resolves as `new_device` with high confidence. Read `is_new_device` / `decision`
for identity trust, not `confidence` alone.

## Run the native server

```bash
cargo run --bin fingerprintd                                   # 127.0.0.1:8080
FP_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9000 cargo run --bin fingerprintd
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
```

Log level is `RUST_LOG` (default `info`).

## Call it from a browser

```ts
import { createCollector, run } from '@cdlab/fingerprintd'

const result = await run({
  baseUrl: 'https://fp.example.com',
  collect: createCollector(),   // FingerprintJS + BotD + integrity probes
})
// Display-only. Send result.request_id to your backend.
```

`getChallenge()` and `identify()` are exported for callers that drive the two
requests themselves. See `packages/client/README.md` for the wire format and the
component schema.

## Configuration

Layered, increasing priority: built-in defaults → `fingerprintd.toml` →
`FP_`-prefixed environment variables. Native-server keys:

- `FP_BIND_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1:8080`) — listen address.
- `FP_NONCE_TTL_SECS` (default `30`) — one-time nonce lifetime.
- `FP_NONCE_MAX_LIVE` (default `1000000`) — cap on live nonces.
- `FP_TRUST_EDGE_HEADERS` (default `false`) — trust edge-injected JA4/IP headers.
- `FP_INTEGRITY_PENALTY_ENABLED` (default `false`) — let a `noise` integrity
  verdict lower confidence (always surfaced).
- `FP_TS_SKEW_SECS` (default `30`) — allowed request `ts` skew; the window is
  always enforced.
- `FP_FUZZY_MAX_RECORDS` (default `1000000`) — max distinct visitors.
- `FP_FUZZY_RECORD_TTL_SECS` (default `0`, disabled) — evict unseen records.
- `FP_FUZZY_MAX_BLOCK` (default `1024`) — per-block visitor cap.
- `FP_FUZZY_MAX_FREQUENCY_VALUES` (default `1000000`) — tracked `u_i` value cap.
- `FP_FUZZY_MAX_AGREEMENT_COMPONENTS` (default `1024`) — tracked `m_i` component cap.
- `FP_ADMIN_KEY` (unset) — Bearer key gating `DELETE /visitor/{visitor_id}`.
- `FP_API_KEY` (unset) — Bearer key gating `GET /events/{request_id}`.
- `FP_EVENT_TTL_SECS` (default `3600`) — stored identify event lifetime.
- `FP_EVENT_MAX` (default `100000`) — stored identify event cap.
- `FP_RETENTION_SECS` (default `0`, disabled) — purge records not seen for this long.
- `FP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default `10`) — per-request deadline (`408`).
- `FP_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` (default `1024`) — global concurrency cap.

The `admin_key` / `api_key` controls are fail-closed and off by default — each
endpoint activates only once its key is set. The native store is in-memory and
process-local (a restart re-mints devices); the edge Worker persists to libSQL
(default) or D1 and has its own configuration (`apps/edge/README.md`).

## Trust boundaries (do not misreport as vulnerabilities)

- Passive signals (JA4/IP) are read server-side from the connection, never from the
  client body, and only when the deployment trusts the edge (`trust_edge_headers`
  natively; Cloudflare's own `request.cf` on the edge Worker).
- The browser-side `/identify` response is display-only by design; integrators
  must gate on `GET /events/{request_id}`. No secret ships to the client.
- The integrity probes, `botd` and `user_agent` are client-reported risk signals;
  a sophisticated adversary forging a single signal is a documented limitation.

## Design

`DESIGN.md` is the authoritative spec: architecture (§1–§9) and fuzzy-matching
engine (§1–§12). Source doc-comments reference its sections as `architecture §N` /
`fuzzy-matching §N`. Read it before proposing changes to the matching model, the
challenge-response split, the passive-signal trust boundary, or the HTTP contract.
